Government plays hardly a role at all but will definitely tax the hell out of everyone.

[quote=shahzada;58225127][b]Question of the Day #22:[/b]

What is the government?s role in the economy?

[i]This is an automated message.[/i][/quote]

1.Central Control: The government maintains centralized oversight and management of the economy.
2.Nationalization: Key industries and natural resources are owned by the state.
3.Social Programs: Healthcare, education, and housing services are provided to support the populace.
4.Worker Support: The rights and benefits of workers are guaranteed.
5.Infrastructure Development: Investment is made in transportation and energy infrastructure.
6.Support for Local Industries: Assistance is provided to small businesses and local producers.

[quote=shahzada;58225127][b]Question of the Day #22:[/b]

What is the government?s role in the economy?

[i]This is an automated message.[/i][/quote]

The government influences the national economy in a number of ways.

1. Grants and Subsidies: The government when the nation annexes new territory, will grant specific companies resource rights to the land to help create new jobs and kickstart the economy of the area (companies are chosen at random, or to make or more competitive market)

2. Military spending: The government buys its tanks and schout vehicles from the UREV, yes, but it also produces things like small arms, ammunition, ships, aircraft, and many more domestically! Along with fuel production for the multitude of vehicles that keep the military going, the military buys as many things domestically as possible to not only invest in the nation, but further modernize itself and the economy!

3. Regulation: Like any good government, the ULR regulates workplace safety, food items, wage, and all that fun stuff. The regulation isn't too overbearing, although some unscrupulous businessmen would say otherwise.

4. Education: The government does offer free college through the military if you wish to become an officer or specialist, but they instead encourage those in the national guard after they graduate high school to attend trade school, which is funded by the government and thus free.

5. Limits on allowed foreign investment: Although foreign investment is allowed, if a company is sizable enough to fall under the "National industry" label, foreign investment is capped at 40% of the company.

6. Investment in infrastructure: The government is keen on providing ample routes of transportation and modern energy plants. This keeps construction companies busy, while also providing new jobs to help run everything constructed.

7. Shipbuilding: As the ULR is a major trade hub between continents, it serves as a convenient place to buy and build ships. The government regularly makes deals for resources, weapons, or just plain old cash for military and cargo ships with other nations. Companies are also free to order whatever ships they want, of course.
